history.period: Legendary Treta Yuga origins; elevated under the Perumals and Zamorins (medieval)
history.summary: Hilltop shrine at West Hill, Kozhikode, held by tradition to be the 108th and last Devi temple consecrated by Parasurama, who is said to have ploughed the rocky site to invoke Goddess Durga and performed the first Vaavu Bali here. The temple declined after its founding; the Perumals restored daily worship and raised it to Mahakshetra status, and the Zamorins later renovated it into its present form. It remains managed by the Zamorin family. Compound features a rock-cut pond and a natural cave (Guhas) used in the Devi's rituals; the temple is a noted stop on the Dakshin pilgrimage and for Sabarimala-bound devotees.

name: Varakkal Devi Temple
town_description: Kozhikode (Calicut) is a historic port city on Kerala's Malabar Coast, once the capital of the Zamorins and the famed City of Spices visited by Vasco da Gama in 1498. Today it is the commercial and cultural heart of North Kerala, known for its beaches, backwaters, and culinary heritage. The temple sits atop a hillock at West Hill, about 4 km from the city centre, overlooking the Arabian Sea.

travel.road: On Varakkal Temple Road, West Hill, near NH-766; reachable by town bus, auto-rickshaw, or taxi from Kozhikode city

visitor_information.best_time: Throughout the year; busiest during Navarathri (September-October) and the Vavu Bali days
